english_text: Mr President , the conclusion of trade negotiations between the European Union and Mexico , considered from a positive perspective , could mean a new and durable framework for the institutionalisation of political dialogue and cooperation , provided that this trade pact works to the benefit of both sides . Unfortunately , the experience of NAFTA shows us that this target was not achieved automatically , because there is evidence that free trade has had an adverse effect on the lives of many people , exacerbated environmental damage , and marginalised wide sections of the Mexican population - all the more so as Mexican human rights NGOs have also reported a deterioration in the human rights situation since the interim agreement came into force in 1998 . So , all in all , the on-going agreement has not allowed Mexico to protect vulnerable labour , intensive sectors and minimal environmental standards . In the light of this we can not be optimistic , because the procedure followed in the recent negotiations , without effective control either in this House or in the Mexican Senate , provides ample evidence that the agreement lacks those mechanisms absolutely necessary to ensure that the damage currently being done will not be repeated again in the future .
